# Renovatio Imperii

**Version 1.2** · for Crusader Kings III 1.20.* · [Steam Workshop](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3806764786) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [All versions](https://github.com/nchelix/ck3-mods-public/releases?q=renovatio-imperii&expanded=true)

Rome fell centuries ago, but its inheritance never found an owner. Vanilla
makes that inheritance a trophy: you cannot even see the decision to restore
the Roman Empire until you already hold e_byzantium and completely control
fourteen Mediterranean duchies, and the reconquest casus belli requires you
to already be Roman emperor before you can use it.

That is backwards. Charlemagne did not wait to be emperor before he called
himself one. Neither did the Ottonians, the Bulgarian tsars, or the Ottomans
after them. They proclaimed first and spent their reigns making it true.

**This mod lets you do the same. You do not get the empire. You get a claim,
an identity, and a great many enemies.**

---

## Proclaim Heir to Rome

A decision, not a cheat button. It is only available to a ruler of king tier
or higher, it costs a genuine fortune in prestige, and it is gated on
plausibility: either your culture descends from Rome (Latin or Byzantine
heritage), or you hold at least one county from the old Empire's
Mediterranean or Iberian heartland. A duke in Connacht does not get to be
Augustus.

Proclaim, and you gain the **Roman Claimant** trait -- prestige and
influence income, a strong bond with fellow claimants, better standing with
your vassals -- and the **Renovatio Imperii** casus belli against former
Roman land, adapted from vanilla's own reconquest CB but open to a claimant
rather than to an emperor. What you do not gain is any land at all. The
empire still has to be won.

## The world does not shrug

This is the actual point of the mod. The claim is cheap to make and
expensive to hold, because everyone with a stake in the old Roman name has
an opinion about a newcomer claiming it, and it shows up in your opinion
breakdown with a reason attached, not as an invisible number.

| Reactor | Opinion | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Constantinople | **-40** | There cannot be two Romes. |
| The Holy Roman Emperor | **-30** | A rival claimant, and they were first. |
| The Papacy | conditional | Court him and coronation follows. Bypass him and it does not. |
| Latin and Byzantine cultures | **+15** | A plausible restorer. |
| Everyone else | **-10**, fading | Presumption. |

## Six events, not one acknowledge button

- **The Proclamation** -- how you frame it in the moment shapes who
  hears a restoration and who hears an insult.
- **Word Reaches Constantinople** -- the Byzantine emperor writes back,
  unimpressed, and does not bother threatening you.
- **The Pope's Offer** -- coronation in exchange for concessions. Accept
  for legitimacy at a price, or refuse and answer to no one.
- **Antiquarians and Senators** -- genealogists, self-declared senators,
  and the occasional fraud turn up at your court wanting to serve a restored
  Rome that does not exist yet.
- **A Rival Claimant** -- an AI ruler proclaims too. Two heirs to the
  same dead empire is a contradiction the world notices.
- **Judgement** -- a reckoning of how far the claim actually went:
  pretender, regional power, or genuinely restored.

## AI rulers can proclaim too

Rarely, and weighted toward rulers it would actually make sense for --
existing emperors, high prestige, Byzantine cultural heritage -- and capped
at one claimant in the world at a time. A rival claim is meant to be an
event you react to, not weather.

## You can fail

Proclaiming grants a claim, not land. If you cannot make it stick, you die a
pretender, which is the honest outcome for most rulers who reach for Rome.
Vanilla's own restoration decisions are completely untouched: they still
exist, still work, and are still the actual finish line. This mod is the
road there, not a replacement for it.

## Compatibility

- Built and tested against **CK3 1.19 "Scribe"**.
- **Ironman and achievements:** this mod will disable achievements, as
  gameplay mods do.
- **Other mods:** adds one trait, one casus belli, one decision, five
  opinion modifiers and six events, and overwrites no base game file.
- **Existing saves:** safe to add mid-game. Remove the mod and any
  character holding the Roman Claimant trait simply loses it; a war already
  fought over the Renovatio Imperii casus belli is unaffected.

## Languages

Available in all nine languages the game supports. English is fully
written; the other eight currently show the English wording. Translations
are welcome.

## Install

- **Steam Workshop:** subscribe on the Workshop page above.
- **Manually, any version:** download `renovatio-imperii-v<version>.zip` from the [releases](https://github.com/nchelix/ck3-mods-public/releases?q=renovatio-imperii&expanded=true) and extract it into `Documents/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/`, then enable it in the launcher.
